items.defectStatement: parseRefreshTokenResponse inserts the literal "refresh_token" when a normal provider response omits refresh_token. Office365 merges this into its stored credentials, replacing the valid refresh token and breaking subsequent refreshes.
obligations: Do not synthesize a refresh token in the non-sharing parsing branch.
Preserve a refresh token supplied by the parsed response.
Retain placeholder behavior for the sharing/sync branch.
items.notes: Use both conditions selecting the minimum-schema branch; checking only the sharing flag is insufficient.

items.defectStatement: Salesforce getClient unconditionally refreshes OAuth credentials and attempts a database update even when the stored access token is valid. This adds unnecessary network work and failure paths, including rejection of successful responses with an empty statusText, while the connection still receives the original credentials.
obligations: Constructing a client with valid stored credentials must not trigger an OAuth refresh or credential write.
Preserve connection construction using the stored instance URL, access token, refresh token, and app configuration.
Remove the unconditional refresh request's dependency on statusText being "OK".
items.notes: Deleting the added block restores the prior connection path and fixes the gold regression. Implementing sync-aware refresh is a broader enhancement; deletion does not implement it.

items.defectStatement: The webhook lets body-schema validation errors escape, producing server errors for malformed requests. Decryption and JSON parsing of keys also throw without handling, so invalid encrypted payloads have the same problem.
obligations: Return HTTP 400 when the request body fails the declared schema.
Return HTTP 400 for undecryptable keys or decrypted content that is invalid JSON.
Stop invalid requests before credential writes.
Preserve authorization checks and normal credential creation/update behavior for valid requests.
items.notes: This exact-anchor fix prevalidates keys; the unchanged later code decrypts them again. A safeParse-only replacement fixes the narrower finding but not the gold description's decryption/JSON errors. Avoiding duplicate decryption requires a wider edit.

items.defectStatement: Google Calendar persists the entire successful parse result, { success, data }, as credential.key instead of the parsed credentials. Subsequent initialization expects token fields at the top level and fails schema validation.
obligations: Persist the parsed credential data rather than the parse-result wrapper.
Update the same credential record and preserve the surrounding refresh flow.
items.notes: The closing update-call delimiter is outside the anchor and must remain there. Independent problems in the shared parser are outside this finding.
